The mirtverse agent for Claude

Source: vignettes/articles/mirtverse-agent.Rmd
mirtverse-agent.Rmd

The mirtverse agent is Claude working as a psychometrician on your computer. You put your data in a folder, open the folder in Claude Code, and ask in plain words:

Analyze exam.csv. It is a 40-item end-of-year math test taken by 1,200 grade 8 students. The lang column says whether a student is an English language learner.

Claude reads the data, fits and compares IRT models with mirtverse and mirt, checks every item, tests the items for DIF across lang, scores the students, looks at the plots, and explains the results in plain language. It writes the scores, plots and an HTML report to a mirtverse-output folder, together with an R script that reproduces every step. You do not need to know R, but everything it does is R code you can check and rerun.

It is not a chatbot that answers from memory. Every number comes from mirtverse running on your data, on your computer.

How it works

The plugin gives Claude three things:

  • Tools. An MCP server, mv_agent_server(), runs in R and gives Claude tools to read your data, fit models, check items, test DIF, score people, draw plots, interpret results, write a report, save the script, and run other R code. (MCP is the standard way AI assistants connect to tools.)
  • Skills. Instructions that tell Claude how a careful psychometrician works: Check the data first, explain the model choice, discuss every flagged item with its evidence, separate statistical from practical DIF, and never invent a number.
  • An analyst agent. A subagent that runs a whole analysis by itself, so Claude can analyze several files or subgroups side by side.
Skill Ask for example
analyze-test “Analyze exam.csv”, “Calibrate this test”, “Is this test any good?”
check-dif “Are any items unfair to English language learners?”
review-items “Which items should we revise before next year?”
write-report “Write up the results for the school board”
setup “The mirtverse tools are missing”

Claude picks the skill from your request; you can also call one directly, for example /mirtverse:check-dif.

Install

You need three things on your computer.

  1. R (4.1 or later) from CRAN.

  2. mirtverse. In R:

    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/mirtverse")

  3. Claude Code. Follow the installation guide; it runs in a terminal, in the Claude desktop app, and in VS Code and JetBrains.

Then add the plugin. In Claude Code, type:

/plugin marketplace add okanbulut/mirtverse
/plugin install mirtverse@mirtverse

(Recent versions of Claude Code also accept /plugin install mirtverse --marketplace okanbulut/mirtverse in one step.)

Finally, connect the mirtverse server, once. The plugin brings the skills and the analyst agent; the tools come from the MCP server in the mirtverse package, which runs on your computer and is connected separately. In a terminal, run:

claude mcp add --scope user mirtverse -- Rscript -e "mirtverse::mv_agent_server()"

(If Rscript is not on your PATH, which is common on Windows, run mirtverse::mv_mcp_config(NULL, client = "claude-code", mode = "analysis") in R; it prints the same command with the full path to Rscript. You can also just ask Claude to “set up mirtverse”: the setup skill walks through it.) Restart Claude Code, and the mirtverse tools are ready in every folder you open.

Use it

  1. Put your data file in a folder, for example ~/projects/math-test. CSV, Excel, SPSS, Stata and R files work.
  2. Open the folder in Claude Code (in a terminal: cd ~/projects/math-test then claude).
  3. Ask. Say what the test is and what you need, the way you would brief a colleague. Claude asks if something is unclear, such as which columns are items or whether 9 means “not answered”.

A typical exchange, here on the SAT12 data that ship with mirt (the numbers are what the tools return):

You: Analyze the SAT12 data from mirt. The answer key is 1, 4, 5, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 4, 2, 1, 5, 3, 4, 4, 1, 4, 3, 3, 4, 1, 3, 5, 1, 3, 1, 5, 4, 5, and 8 means not answered.

Claude: (describes the data, scores the responses with the key, fits the Rasch, 2PL and 3PL models, checks the items, then) The 2PL model is the best choice: Its BIC is 111 points lower than the Rasch model’s, and the 3PL model did not converge. The test works reasonably well (RMSEA .028, CFI .954) and its reliability is .84, adequate for reporting individual scores. Nine of the 32 items are flagged. Item.32 barely separates weaker from stronger students (discrimination 0.12) and its location, 14.2, is far beyond anyone who took the test, so check its key first … The files are in mirtverse-output/: Scores, plots, model-report.html, and analysis.R, which reproduces everything.

You can keep going: “Drop Q17 and compare”, “Check DIF by school”, “Make the report for teachers, not psychometricians”.

The built-in datasets work too, so you can try it without data of your own, for example “Fit a graded model to the Science data”.

What the tools do

Tool What it does
project_overview Data files, models fitted so far, and output files
describe_dataset Columns, item types, missing values, likely IDs and groups
fit_model Fits a model or compares models (select_model()), with missing codes and answer keys
check_items Item statistics, fit and flags (item_table())
check_dif DIF tests and effect sizes (dif())
score_people Ability estimates and standard errors, written to a CSV
plot_model Item curves, information, Wright map, item fit, scores, DIF; Claude sees the picture
interpret_model Plain-language interpretation (interpret())
write_report HTML technical report (mv_report())
save_script The R code of every step, as one script
run_r Any other R code, in the same session
guide, mirtverse_help The analysis guides and the mirtverse help pages

Fitted models are kept between sessions (in .mirtverse-mcp/models), so you can come back tomorrow and ask “Write the report for yesterday’s model”.

Your data

The analysis runs on your computer. Your data files are only read, never changed, and results go to mirtverse-output/. What Claude sees is what the tools return: Column summaries, model and item statistics, plots and interpretations, not the full data. Code that Claude runs with run_r can print rows of the data, so for sensitive data tell Claude not to print individual records, or remove names and IDs before you start. Your organization’s rules for AI tools apply.

Without the plugin

A CLAUDE.md for one folder. mv_agent_init() writes the two files that turn a folder into a mirtverse project for Claude Code: A CLAUDE.md with the agent’s instructions, and a .mcp.json that starts the server with the full path to Rscript. This is also the way to go on Windows when Rscript is not on the PATH.

mirtverse::mv_agent_init("~/projects/math-test",
                         title = "Grade 8 math test, spring 2026")

Open CLAUDE.md and fill in the “About this project” section (what the test measures, who took it, what the results are for); Claude reads it at the start of every session. Then start Claude Code in the folder and approve the mirtverse server.

Claude Desktop and other assistants. The same server works with any MCP client. mv_mcp_config() prints the settings:

mv_mcp_config("~/projects/math-test", client = "claude-desktop", mode = "analysis")
mv_mcp_config("~/projects/math-test", client = "codex", mode = "analysis")

The skills are written for Claude Code, but the server carries its own guides (guide("analysis") and guide("interpreting")) and three prompts, “Analyze my test”, “Check items for fairness” and “Write a technical report”, so other clients get the same workflow.
